title: Cycle publish fails uploading third blind preview to production storage
description:
## Observed behavior

Authenticated `apricity cycle publish` creates/uses the incumbent and uploads preview options A and B, then deterministically fails while uploading option C with a generic `service error`. No `ListeningCycle` record is written, leaving the Lab unable to present the intended three-option blind comparison.

## Reproducer

1. Log in as a production user who can create Scores and Labs (`apricity whoami` returns `ryan@anth.us`).
2. Run `apricity cycle publish` with an incumbent and two `--candidate <APR> <M4A>` options (three total blind options).
3. Observe failure at `cycles/us-east-1:4e0950fc-fd10-cd29-df2a-3e6182f0d84b/cyc_<id>/C.m4a` with `could not upload ...: service error`.
4. Repeat: the same third-option failure occurs with a new cycle ID.

The M4A files are valid, small (565–758 KB), and the failure is independent of their source recordings. Cognito/AppSync authentication is established: `whoami`, hidden incumbent Score creation, and `lab start` all succeed in the same session.

## Expected behavior

A cycle with an incumbent plus two candidates uploads all A/B/C preview audio, writes exactly one open `ListeningCycle` record, and can be attached to a Lab.

## Definition of done

- Surface the underlying storage error without exposing credentials.
- Correct the production upload/configuration/authorization defect so A, B, C, and D option keys upload for authenticated authorized users.
- Make publish atomic or perform compensating cleanup: on failure, do not leave orphan candidate Scores or uploaded objects.
- Add an integration test using a fake/object-store boundary that proves a three-option cycle writes A/B/C and its `ListeningCycle`; add a failure-path test proving cleanup and actionable diagnostics.
- Confirm a production smoke test can publish and attach a three-option cycle to `lab_403470bc015eefd2`.

## Out of scope

This is not a Cognito login issue and does not change the blind-lettered cycle design.

comments.author: home
comments.text: Bringing this production cycle-publish failure into the current work. I will trace the exact A/B/C object upload path, surface the storage cause, implement rollback for partially uploaded objects and candidate Scores, add fake-store success/failure coverage, then run the production smoke specified here using the provided Lab ID.

comments.author: home
comments.text: Reproduced the production failure with the authorized smoke publish on 2026-09-28. AWS returned AccessDenied for s3:PutObject under files/cycles/<identity>/<cycle>/A.wav: the signed-in user assumed the membersGroupReadOnly role, which had no write policy for cycle files. The publish compensation removed the partial candidate Scores; no ListeningCycle was created. Added code changes on codex/apricitus-af4eba to report safe S3 service details, stage local files before mutations, and compensate partial writes. Added an identity-scoped IAM grant for members/curators group roles (S3 object ARN uses cognito-identity.amazonaws.com:sub) so it does not grant cross-user writes. Focused Rust and policy tests pass. Post-fix production smoke is pending deployment; deploys run through the repository release flow.

comments.author: home
comments.text: Implementation is ready for review in https://github.com/AnthusAI/Apricity/pull/57. Focused Rust rollback/publish tests and the identity-scoped IAM policy test pass. The production smoke is intentionally not repeated until the storage policy change is deployed.
